title: Philips Hue Bridge Pro Smart Accessory $117.50 + Delivery ($0 with OnePass/C&C/in Store) @ Bunnings Warehouse
body:
Deal: Philips Hue Bridge Pro Smart Accessory $117.50 + Delivery ($0 with OnePass/C&C/in Store) @ Bunnings Warehouse

[281982] Has anyone upgraded from the standard Hue bridge & noticed much of a difference? I have an outdoor Hue LED strip for the pool area & has been quite intermittent with the standard bridge, was wondering if I’d fare better with this one?
[A 1] The hue globes mesh together to create the network, if there's an existing light fitting suitably placed at your house (like back veradah or similar), you could install a hue globe there which might allow a stronger connection to your pool area, which may solve the issue for you.
I've got globes at the very rear of my yard and never had any connection issues, but, I have about 40+ globes throughout so maybe that's why.
[Alx75] I've transferred three v2 Bridges onto a single Pro. I can't say I see any difference in how fast the lights react because it was always instant for me, never had any issues with old bridges. As the other comment mentioned, the more lights you have, the stronger the mesh network is, and I have a LOT of lights. I would definitely recommend getting this one for this price, even if you're just going to keep it in the box for when you actually need it.
[ONEMariachi] I moved from the original because i was getting drop outs, slowdowns and issues syncing properly with apple home. New bridge has been flawless for the past 4-5 months now.

It still needs power though (USB-C), so not sure what you're saying there…
[cerealJay] motion aware feature
Some drawbacks:
You need at least 3 globes in any given area, even a small room.
If you want the security feature it's a paid subscription. This is terrible given the processing happens locally and all you need is an alert sent.
It uses triangulation of the RF signal. It can pick up "motion" through walls.
Big delay compared with proper motion sensors. Enter room…. wait…. wait… lights on.
[A 1] If you want the security feature it's a paid subscription.
Cheers for that info, personally my only use case would be the security feature (I don't really use the light sensor function). I'm really annoyed they have pay walled the alert, what a joke, guess I'll stick to using the dedicated motion sensors for alerts. Unless the bridge pro pay walls that too, in which case I'm returning it I think.
[Blitzfx] I was reading reviews of that feature and users said that often, the lights would only turn on after taking a few steps into a dark room vs having a dedicated motion sensor.
Some said it doesn't detect movement if you're sitting down watching TV or eating etc, and it wouldn't reactivate if they waved their arms.
The technology works by sensing differences in the signal disruption between devices, which explains why people are seeing it behave the way it does.
